scope: Proposition 6.3 (A fixed gap with adjustable completeness) of the manuscript “The Unique Games Theorem” (preprints/The-Unique-Games-Theorem-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 102 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 04d0290a9cb7ee81), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 36. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix p∗ > 0 and choose the latent and shortcode data in the order of Equation (5.4). For every sufficiently large cube k, the matrix game G constructed from a weighted parity instance E with distinct positions satisfies OPT(E) ≥ 1 − ξ =⇒ val(G) ≥ 1 − kξ − p∗/2, OPT(E) ≤ 4/5 =⇒ val(G) ≤ 99/100. The lower threshold on k depends only on the fixed latent and shortcode data, not on E or ξ.
